unit.title: Compiler Frontend Kickoff: Engineering a MiniCOOL-0 Lexer
unit.scope: Specify, implement, test, and explain a deterministic lexer for the manager-defined MiniCOOL-0 subset. The unit introduces the compiler pipeline but does not include parsing, semantic analysis, optimization, code generation, MIPS, or an official COOL assignment.
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student who knows basic computer architecture and can build a nontrivial program in Java or C++.
learning_objectives: Translate a lexical contract into a deterministic scanner with explicit states and source positions.
Apply maximal munch and precedence rules without losing linear-time behavior.
Separate scanning logic, diagnostics, command-line I/O, and tests behind stable interfaces.
Build reproducible automated tests for normal, boundary, and malformed inputs.
Use concrete repository evidence to justify correctness and design decisions.
learner_deliverables: A Java or C++ MiniCOOL-0 lexer with the command-line behavior specified in student_safe/STUDY_TASK.md.
A deterministic automated test suite and documented build/test commands.
A concise engineering README or DESIGN document.

unit_completion_requires: All required deliverables are present in the learner submission.
The documented clean build and automated test commands succeed under the worker harness.
An independent validator applies examiner_only/RUBRIC.md to repository evidence and records a passing result.
completion_policy.unit_pass_threshold: 70/100 with every essential-behavior gate in the rubric satisfied
completion_policy.promotion_authority: Only a validator controlled by the worker harness may mark this unit complete.
completion_policy.course_completion: Completion of this kickoff unit is not completion of Stanford CS143, the cataloged set of written assignments or labs, or any broader compiler curriculum. Course completion remains NOT_EVALUATED until later jobs retrieve and validate an authorized full course plan and its required evidence.
